background.source: Water is a crucial compound for all known living organisms, and it plays a major role in the Earth's environment. The chemical formula for water is H2O, consisting of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Water is nearly colorless, odorless, and tasteless. It is found in all three states of matter: solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapor or steam). Most of the water on earth is found in oceans and seas, covering about 71% of the Earth's surface. Freshwater is used mainly for agriculture and industrial processes. Water moves continuously throughout the water cycle of evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, and runoff. The water cycle is responsible for weather patterns such as rain, which can be accumulated in buckets or channeled through pipes. Water is an essential resource for many industries and is also used for recreation and entertainment such as swimming, boating, and skiing.
background.target: Heat is a form of energy that is transferred between a thermodynamic system and its surroundings due to a temperature difference. It can be defined as the difference in internal energy of a system between its final and initial states along with considering the work done in the process. Calorimetry is the process of measuring the transfer of energy through heat, usually measured in joules (J). This concept is applied to various systems including a kettle, iron, and even the sun. Whether it is the transfer of heat to boil water, the conduction of heat through a metal bar, or the heat transferred from the sun to the Earth, heat plays a crucial role in our daily lives and in the functioning of various natural processes.
